title: Draw the frame: a struct on the stack
prompt:
The program is paused inside `scaled_rect`, which keeps an int and a `rect` record in its frame. Fill in where each field sits.

The record's fields are equates counted from the start of the record (`rect_width`, `rect_height`, `rect_area`), and `rect_s` is where the record starts in the frame, so a field's offset from fp is `rect_s` plus the field's own offset. The frames view names each field after the record: `rect_s.rect_width` is the width field.

## What is checked

- the frame's size in bytes
- the offsets from fp of `scale_s`, `rect_s.rect_width`, `rect_s.rect_height` and `rect_s.rect_area`
- the offsets from fp of the saved fp and the saved lr

Check runs the program to the pause and compares each number with the frame the emulator draws there. A wrong number shows a hint, never the answer.
program:
// Build a rectangle record on the stack, scaled up, and print it.

define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

// struct rect { int width; int height; long area; }
rect_width = 0                                  // 4 bytes
rect_height = 4                                 // 4 bytes
rect_area = 8                                   // a long starts on a multiple of 8
rect_size = 16

scale_size = 4                                  // int

scale_s = 16
rect_s = (scale_s + scale_size + 7) & -8        // the record holds a long, so it starts on a multiple of 8
alloc = -(rect_s + rect_size) & -16
dealloc = -alloc

.data
fmt_out:    .string "%d by %d, area %ld\n"

.text

// scaled_rect(w0 = width, w1 = height, w2 = scale): prints the rectangle scaled up
        .balign 4
        .global scaled_rect
scaled_rect:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, alloc]!
        mov     fp, sp

        str     w2, [fp, scale_s]               // keep the scale
        add     x9, fp, rect_s                  // x9 = &rect
        mul     w10, w0, w2
        str     w10, [x9, rect_width]           // rect.width = width * scale
        mul     w11, w1, w2
        str     w11, [x9, rect_height]          // rect.height = height * scale
        sxtw    x12, w10                        // widen before the multiply
        sxtw    x13, w11
        mul     x12, x12, x13
        str     x12, [x9, rect_area]            // rect.area = rect.width * rect.height

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        ldr     w1, [x9, rect_width]
        ldr     w2, [x9, rect_height]
        ldr     x3, [x9, rect_area]
        bl      printf

        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], dealloc
        ret

        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        mov     w0, 3                           // a 3 by 4 rectangle
        mov     w1, 4
        mov     w2, 5                           // scaled up 5 times
        bl      scaled_rect

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret

slots.name: scale_s
slots.hint: scale_s is given as a plain number in the program.

slots.name: rect_s.rect_width
slots.hint: Work out rect_s first: (scale_s + scale_size + 7) & -8 rounds the end of scale_s up to a multiple of 8. The width field is at offset 0 in the record.

slots.name: rect_s.rect_height
slots.hint: rect_height is 4 bytes into the record, so its offset from fp is rect_s + 4.

slots.name: rect_s.rect_area
slots.hint: rect_area is 8 bytes into the record, so its offset from fp is rect_s + 8.

hints.size: The frame holds everything up to the end of the record, rect_s + rect_size, rounded up to the next multiple of 16.
hints.savedFp: stp fp, lr, [sp, alloc]! stores fp first, at the new sp, and mov fp, sp then points fp at that same address.
hints.savedLr: lr is the second of the two registers the stp stores, in the bytes right after the saved fp.
